subject: Post-demo: performance targets, measurement, and SLA language follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Tim O'Connor <tim@cloudbank.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap: performance targets + next steps

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap of what we discussed on the performance front and the open items for the SLO/SLA section in the contract. Please correct me if I've mis-stated anything.

Key targets you requested
- Latency: p95 < 250ms, p99 < 500ms for single-request text-generation (end-to-end)
- Throughput: 200 RPS sustained per region during peak windows; burst to 350 RPS for up to 5 minutes
- Concurrency: support 50 concurrent sessions (long-lived streaming) without queuing beyond 100ms
- Streaming: first-byte streaming time-to-first-byte (TTFB) target 50ms; subsequent token stream steady-state average per-token < 20ms

Open clarifications we agreed to confirm
1) Exact measurement boundary (edge vs. application vs. customer SDK).
2) Treatment of retries, client-side backoff, and warm-up (do you want exclusions?).
3) Reporting cadence (weekly dashboard + monthly SLA summary?) and remedies for missed SLOs.

Next steps
- Vivek will share a short tech note on where we measure latency (edge egress vs. origin) and how streaming is timed. (action: Vivek, by 3/08 EOD)
- Marissa will draft SLO language that matches your procurement template and include an exclusion list. (action: Marissa, by 3/09)
- Sarah (procurement) will confirm if CloudBank requires a monthly PDF SLA report vs. access to a live dashboard.

Attachments: initial SLO language draft + service diagram attached.

Thanks,
Marissa

Tim — quick tech follow-up on measurement methodology so procurement can see the mechanics:  

Measurement summary
- Measurement point: all latency percentiles are measured at the Redwood ingress/egress edge after TLS termination and before any client-side SDK processing. That is the time window we report as "end-to-end" for SLA purposes.
- Percentiles: p50/p90/p95/p99 computed on a rolling 5-minute window for each region; we aggregate daily for dashboard and monthly for SLA compliance checks.
- Streaming: we measure two things — TTFB (time from request accept to first token byte emitted) and per-token delta for the subsequent stream. TTFB target and per-token averages are both computed over the same rolling 5-minute windows.
- Throughput/concurrency: RPS is measured at the edge. Concurrency is measured as concurrent active sessions holding a streaming connection.

Exclusions and normalization
- Warm-up period: we can exclude a configurable warm-up window (default 60s) after a large-scale deployment or capacity scale event.
- Maintenance windows: scheduled maintenance windows agreed in advance are excluded from SLA calculations.
- Client retries: automated client retries within backoff policy will be collapsed when attributed to a single logical request; however, if retries are due to server errors we will count the original request path for SLA metrics.

Reporting & alerts
- Live dashboard: rolling 24h, 7d views with selectable percentiles per model + raw metric export (CSV).
- Weekly digest: auto-email with summary of any percentile breaches and tail-analysis.
- Monthly SLA report: PDF with raw percentile tables, incident notes, and root-cause summaries if any SLA thresholds were missed.

Will attach a one-page note for procurement to reference — see Marissa's attachments. Happy to do a follow-up 15-min call to walk procurement through measurement examples.

Thanks,
Vivek
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai

Thanks — that level of detail is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and engineering here: 

1) Measurement boundary: procurement prefers SLA measured at "customer-facing edge" (i.e., after CDN/edge). Can you confirm Redwood's edge is where the metric is collected, and if there are optional downstream proxies that we run how that affects numbers?

2) Exclusions: curious about how you handle autoscaler-triggered scale events. We need clarity whether short-duration degradations during scaling will be excluded or counted. What's your default policy?

3) Remedies: draft procurement language asks for a service credit scheme and a reporting cadence. They typically ask for a formula (e.g., X% credit per missed SLO period). Are you open to language like that or do you prefer remediation via operational remedies only (e.g., root-cause mitigation and plan)?

Also — is the weekly digest something we can subscribe to as a CSV export? Sarah in procurement will confirm legal wording once we have the measurement section nailed down.

—Tim
Director, Platform Engineering | CloudBank

Hi Tim — looping in Evelyn from CS (that's me) to confirm operational posture and remedies. A few points from the CS and reliability side: 

- Autoscaler behavior: brief degradations during elastic scale-up are normally captured as transient spikes. For the SLO we typically allow one short exclusion per calendar month for scale events initiated by Redwood due to capacity thresholds, but we treat customer-initiated scale events differently (we can agree a warm-up exclusion window if you signal a planned traffic surge). We'll mark the exclusion policy in the draft SLA so procurement can review.

- Remedies: Redwood's standard commercial approach is a credit-based remedy for systemic SLA breaches. Proposed short-form language:
  - If monthly SLA compliance fails for a given region for more than 2 days in the billing month, customer is eligible for a service credit of 5% of monthly service fees for that region per additional day of non-compliance, capped at 50% for the month.
  - For isolated incidents with verifiable root cause and remediation, Redwood will provide incident reports and operational mitigation without automatic credits; credits apply only for repeated systemic failures or missed monthly SLO windows.

We can adjust the percentages but will need procurement signoff. Attached is a one-page summary that maps the measurement method to the credit formula.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Marissa / team — procurement here. We received the measurement note and Evelyn's proposed credit language. A few quick asks before we proceed to redlines: 

1) Please confirm the reporting cadence options we can pick from: (A) live dashboard + weekly CSV digest; (B) live dashboard + monthly PDF SLA report; (C) both weekly CSV and monthly PDF. We prefer (C) but need confirmation CSV contains raw percentile tables (p50/p90/p95/p99) as a CSV export.

2) Can you add explicit language about maintenance windows timing and notice: we typically require 72h notice for scheduled maintenance that would be excluded from SLA calculations.

3) Remedies: procurement will propose alternate credit percentages in redline. We need the mechanism for triggering credit automatically (i.e., auditing math) vs. case-by-case. Are you able to commit to automatic credit awarding based on the monthly measurement?

If you can confirm the above and upload the updated draft, we'll circulate to legal and come back with redlines. Also include the DocuSign envelope link when the SOW is ready.

Regards,
Sarah Lee
Procurement Manager | CloudBank
